sessionStart.prompt: This repository may use the devbook convention: arc42/, domain/, tech/, design/, and ai/, each under .devbook/ (.devbook/arc42 and so on). Treat those folders as task-scoped context, not baseline context: load only the chapters the current task needs, never the whole folder by default. Every file and every addressable chapter in them carries a fenced `meta` block; when you create or edit one, write that block in the same change. A review note is never text in a chapter: it is a comment thread in the host that keeps the chapter's workflow state, read and posted through devbook.decision@1, and chapter-review posts one per objection. `capture-specs` writes no note, and `apply-change` never carries an open one into a change brief: an open question is a reason to stop at the gate, not a line item to implement. An edit to one of these folders follows that folder's own instruction file - devbook-arc42, devbook-domain, devbook-tech, devbook-design, or devbook-ai - plus devbook-chapter-metadata.md, and is routed through the flow that covers the folder when a flow engine is installed: a repo-native flow-* skill first, then the engine's own flow for the folder, and directly under the instruction files when no engine is installed at all. Say which of those answered. Decision records, technical debt records, and blueprints are their own flows and never a plain arc42/ chapter edit. When the task crosses between a chapter and its code - writing a chapter from something already implemented, turning an agreed chapter into implementation work, or asking whether the two still agree - route through capture-specs, apply-change, or verify-change instead; each covers the kinds aggregate, domain-service, feature, setting, actor, building-block, and design-component, decided by the chapter's type, and reads a page's click demo as the demo kind beside it, which only /prototype ever writes. capture-specs reads code and its tests and delivers a capture plan to the person - drafts as a delta against the target file, plus the report table - and writes no chapter itself unless a spec-check binding runs it in write mode, which carries only code-ahead entries in, apply-change derives a change brief and hands it to the code-side flow — a repo-native flow first, then the engine's flow-code, which derives the kind in its first stage, and stops with the brief when no engine is installed — touching no source or test tree itself, verify-change reports the drift verdict and writes nothing. An aggregate is captured and briefed whole - the root plus the entities, value objects, and enums it owns and the domain events it raises - so there is no separate entity, value-object, or domain-event kind; a domain service is its own kind and owns the events it raises itself. Behaviour in a bounded context lives in requirements.md and in the invariants subpage of each domain page - domain.invariants.md, domain.<name>.invariants.md - one rule per chapter: a `### Requirement:` is one SHALL sentence about what the product promises, an `### Invariant:` one claim a type guarantees with the `Enforced at:` line that says where; a requirement carries `#### Scenario:` cases, an invariant is proved by its unit test and carries none. requirements.md and the invariants subpages are titled by kind - # Requirements, # Invariants - and a requirements.<name>.md split by its feature, as every domain/ file but context.md is titled by what it holds, a split file by its chapter, never by the context. They are captured and briefed with the prose chapter they belong to and point at it through `related`; the prose chapters keep why, who, the boundary, the lifecycle, and the language, and no rule stays in them. A repository may provide its own repo-native skills, and those take precedence for the categories they cover. This repository may carry its own procedure skills — run, capture, diagnose, estimate, prototype — each reachable by name on either host. Invoke the skill instead of guessing a command, a URL, or a layout: run builds and launches the application from the repository's recipe at .claude/skills/run-<name>/SKILL.md — Claude Code's own run skill follows it, Copilot reaches it through .github/skills/run — leaves it running, and reports its entry points; capture takes evidence a reviewer can open, one file per checkpoint and per failure, the form named honestly; diagnose finds the cause of an observed issue from logs, traces, and breakpoints without handing the person a debugger, and leaves nothing behind in the change; estimate sizes work in story points off 1/2/3/5/8/13/21 against the repository's own reference examples and names the reference each estimate was compared with; prototype starts only from a design question stated in one sentence, written into the file's demo-meta, and settles it with a throwaway standalone HTML file — a state model with a state panel in the ubiquitous language, free play, and walkthroughs, or structurally different screen variants on the repository's demo template, in its design system and Storybook — or revises an existing demo with its screen ids kept, then gives a one-line answer it never writes into the file, which carries no stage, status, verdict, or page; it is never merged, writes into no .devbook/ folder, and changes no source file. A settled design goes to flow-code, a bug to diagnose. The goal in each wrapper is fixed; the procedure is the repository's — edit .agents/skills/<name>.md, or the run-<name> recipe for run, never the wrapper. A skill that is absent here was not adopted: do without it and say so, never invent the procedure.
